tools.name: trust_score
tools.description:
When to call: before you connect to, install, wire into an agent, or recommend an MCP server, to check what the public record shows about whether it is still maintained. Pass the MCP schema-server id.
Returns: JSON with trust_score (0 to 100 or null), display (score · depth · provisional), depth/dep
Dated schema/tool-count observations for an MCP server (a series when known): first_seen, last_observed, drift events. Facts from the register, not a score.

tools.name: dependency_risk
tools.description: An MCP server's dependencies and their mortality state (dead/dormant counts) from the register. Facts, not a score.

description:
When to call: before you connect to or recommend an MCP server, when you care whether its declared dependencies were observed dead or dormant in the lastseen.dev register.
Returns: dated facts, not a score: depends_on[], dead_dependency_count, dormant_dependency_count, n, provenance. Empty depends_o

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "trust_score" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet:
before: "Derived trust score (0-100) for an MCP server, computed from the lastseen.dev register's dated observations by a published method. The score carries DEPTH (how many of 5 dimensions were computable) BOUND INTO the number as `display`, e.g. '80 · depth 2/5 · provisional' — a depth-2 score answers a na" → after: "When to call: before you connect to, install, wire into an agent, or recommend an MCP server, to check what the public record shows about whether it is still maintained. Pass the MCP schema-server id.
Returns: JSON with trust_score (0 to 100 or null), display (score · depth · provisional), depth/dep"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
